hits.name: Sahil Bloom
hits.text: Harsh truth nobody told you about success: Rent is due every single day.
hits.full_text:
Harsh truth nobody told you about success:

Rent is due every single day.

You never really make it. And coasting isn’t an option. Every single day, you have to fight to keep your seat at the table. Because the day you stop doing the work is the day things start to fall apart.

hits.draft_en:

reply_ideas.reply_text: Writing it by hand changes it for me. The pen is slow enough that the loud version of a thought runs out of steam by the bottom of the page, and whatever's left is usually the real thing.

The version of selling that feels natural to me is just being specific. What it is, who it's for, what it costs. People can smell a hard sell, and they can also tell when you actually believe in the thing.
True, and I think the daily rent can be small. Ten honest minutes on the hard days keeps the seat warm better than one heroic week followed by a crash.
The part nobody mentions is how humbling it is. An idea that sounded brilliant in my head falls apart in two sentences on paper, and that's exactly why it works.
